## 2. The new two-actuator query succeeded

The executed source has **35 sites, four reservoir contacts, three installed source actuators and 31 unrefreshed bulk sites**.

The earlier conservative analysis could not certify positive delivery with only two sources enabled. Its best pair had lower current bound **−0.0702577935**. I preserved that failure.

The sharper residual bound and exact binomial inversion made the **same retained probe and isolated-control data** sufficient. No new calibration was acquired, and neither the earlier all-on observations nor the later pair observations entered the new certificate.

The selected pair was control indices \([0,2]\), corresponding to physical source sites \([1,3]\). Before its deployment, the certified stationary net product current was

\[
\boxed{J\in[0.0356208652,\;0.5616139147]}
\]

on the declared simultaneous **95% model-confidence event**. Selection maximized the certified lower bound; it did not establish which pair has the highest true current.

The actual saved state and random-generator state then continued from native time **750,000 to 1,000,000**.

| Quantity | Completed pair run |
|---|---:|
| Native duration | 250,000 |
| Output occupancy observations | 62,500 |
| Occupied output observations | 39,578 |
| Occupancy-based current estimate | 0.266496 |
| Held-out stationary-current interval | [0.1962812354, 0.3367107646] |
| Integrated net product delivered | **67,046 particles** |
| Integrated product divided by duration | 0.268184 |

The occupancy estimate and integrated transition count are different finite-run statistics. Both are consistent with the positive prediction.

The confidence event covers the memory certificate and stationary means. **The realized product count is not a separate 95% guarantee of finite-time payback.**

## 4. The foundational consequence is a separation of local and global memory

The hidden bulk can be enlarged behind the same weak connection while retaining the same small set of observed ports.

If \(L\) unrefreshed bulk sites communicate through a neck of rate \(\gamma\), comparing initially full and initially empty bulk configurations gives

\[
t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\epsilon)
\geq \frac{(1-2\epsilon)L}{2\gamma},
\qquad 0<\epsilon<\frac12.
\]

Thus global state mixing becomes arbitrarily slow as the bulk grows.

Meanwhile, the local reference-memory bound at the accessible ports remains uniformly small. For the constructed family, at time \(4\) its analytical upper bound is below **0.001584**, independently of bulk size. The finite measured bound in the executed source is looser—at most **0.020017435**—and is the bound actually used by the learner.

This establishes a concrete possibility: **a local intervention prediction can be certified while the hidden system retains substantial global memory.** It does not make the bulk material free, and it does not make local throughput grow with that material.

I checked the suggested functional-inequalities paper. Its general-reference inequalities are useful, but its effective generator in Eq. 50 still requires full stationary conditional measures. This construction avoids supplying those conditionals by accepting a narrower target and stronger transport structure. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

## 5. The strongest ordinary comparator still wins for one target

Single-trajectory identification and data-dependent mixing certificates already exist. The present work should not be represented as discovering that learning without repeated resets is possible. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

For one already specified operating setting, **direct acquisition is cheaper and yields a stronger interval**.

For example, directly measuring all-on after the same boundary probe would require:

- **200,000 native time units**, versus **500,000** for the reusable acquisition before its first deployment.
- **125,000 scalar reads**, versus **500,000**.

Those are resource counts for a defined comparator protocol; that alternative was not separately executed. Moreover, all-on is already optimal by monotonicity when enabling sources carries no penalty.

## Verification and preservation

The original record passed its **75-check** receiving audit. The refined result passed a separate **54-check** audit that independently reconstructed the exact binomial tails, concentration inequality, rational optimization endpoints and commitment chain. A separate ledger implementation reproduced the complete chemical totals and exact particle balances.

A fresh-directory replay reproduced the refined certificate, contract and selected controls **byte for byte**, using only the public contract and retained probe and isolated observations. It copied no hidden configuration or joint-run data.

The archive preserves the earlier DAC bounds and rejected configurations, autonomous-control results and failed shortcut, and the intervention-composition work. The new positive certificate, the failed conservative certificate, the more expensive two-actuator operation and the unresolved physical costs remain separately identifiable.
